title: The Bulk Buying Trap

copy.headline: Buying in bulk saves you money.
copy.body: Unless you throw half of it away.

copy.headline: The unit price on a 5 lb bag of spinach is 40% lower than the 5 oz container.
items: But the average person uses 30% of the bag before it goes bad. The actual cost per usable ounce is higher.

copy.headline: Costco's business model depends on this math.
copy.body: The membership fee is subsidized by the assumption that you'll overbuy perishables. Rotisserie chicken at $4.99 gets you in the door. The $14 bag of avocados you throw half of covers the margin.

copy.headline: The breakeven question:
items: Before buying bulk produce, ask: "Will I use 100% of this before it spoils?"
If the answer is no, the smaller size is cheaper.

copy.headline: Bulk buying works for:
copy.body: dry goods, frozen items, canned foods, cleaning supplies — anything with a shelf life measured in months, not days.

copy.headline: Bulk buying fails for:
items: leafy greens, berries, fresh herbs, bread, dairy, and any produce you "might" use.
